h: Getting Ready for Exeter's New Oche
p: Until the doors are open, the best thing you can do is keep an eye on Flight Club's own announcements for the confirmed opening date and booking details. New venues tend to be popular in their first few weeks, and Exeter's big student population and busy Christmas party season mean the early slots could go quickly. If you're planning a festive work do or a birthday, it's worth being ready to book as soon as dates are confirmed.

In the meantime, you could always brush up on your technique. The basic idea is simple: stand side-on to the board with your leading foot forward, keep your elbow still and throw with a smooth flick of the forearm. Release the dart and let your hand follow through towards the target. Don't try to throw too hard. Accuracy beats power every time.

Exeter has plenty to keep you busy while you wait. Large stretches of the Roman and medieval city walls survive and can be followed on foot around the centre, and Northernhay Gardens, right by Queen Street, is a pretty green space beneath the old castle walls. The Underground Passages beneath the city are a unique tour, taking you through medieval tunnels that once carried water. And Gandy Street, a quirky little lane full of independent shops and cafés, is a great spot for a browse.
